newsitem.title: UK: JAPAN REPORT BOOSTS DOLLAR, EUROBOURSES MIXED.
newsitem.headline: JAPAN REPORT BOOSTS DOLLAR, EUROBOURSES MIXED.

text.p: A weak survey of Japanese business sentiment boosted the dollar on Wednesday and European bourses opened mixed, with London and Frankfurt up, helped by a firm Wall Street, but Paris down on currency and strike worries.

At 0900 GMT the dollar was trading at around 108.35 yen, up from its European close on Tuesday of 107.55 after the Bank of Japan's quarterly corporate survey, or "tankan", showed the diffusion index for major manufacturers -- an important gauge of business sentiment -- falling to minus seven in August from minus three in the previous survey in May.
The unexpected figures convinced markets that Japanese interest rates would stay at rock-bottom levels -- weakening the yen. The Japanese discount rate is currently at a record low of 0.5 percent.
The BOJ sought to put the best face on the data which defied economists' predictions of improving sentiment and was the first decline in business sentiment in a year.
A BOJ spokesman said "the doors to the recovery have not been shut...the recovery is still continuing." These remarks gave the yen was some backbone and it drifted off its overnight lows.
Dealers said it would be hard for the dollar to break higher against the yen and it was likely to trade in narrow ranges for the rest of the day.
"The Tankan should put off a BOJ rate rise for a few months which will give support to dollar/yen, but the dollar is facing tough technical barriers," said Tony Norfield at ABN AMRO.
The dollar struggled at minor resistance around 108.40, close to its overnight high, ahead of a bigger hurdle at 108.70, the peak of last week.
On the European bourses, London shares started slightly higher after modest overnight gains in U.S. shares and bonds sparked an early mark-up in prices.

One focus was British Airways stocks, which eased on fears the cancellation of "open skies" talks between the U.S. Transportation Department and the British government could jeopardise its tie-up with American Airlines.
The conclusion of an open skies agreement had been made a prerequisite of the proposed link-up by the U.S.
In Frankfurt firmer German debt and the higher close on Wall Street overnight gave German equities a boost early on, but dealers said the soft dollar/mark still weighed on sentiment.
By contrast the Paris bourse ignored Wall Street and opened lower due to renewed pressure on the franc and growing worries about possible strike action in the autumn.
Dealers said shares were also affected by a slippage in bond prices due to lower than expected June industrial production, showing the economy was still faltering.
CURRENCIES AT 0900 GMT
The dollar was at 108.35 yen and 1.4785 marks compared with Tuesday's European close of 107.78 yen and 1.4779 marks
STOCK MARKETS AT 0900 GMT
London,s FTSE 100 index was up 5.9 at 3911.6.
Frankfurt,s DAX index was up 8.2 at 2567.04.
The Paris CAC-40 was down 8.35 at 2009.64.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold opened firmer at $388.80 versus the London close on Tuesday of 388.55. Silver was also a shade firmer at $5.25.
